 JJ Gabriel (left) could soon be working under José Mourinho at Real Madrid. | Zohaib Alam/Manchester United/Getty Images (Gabriel), Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty Images (Mourinho) Where Does Wantaway Man Utd Wonderkid JJ Gabriel Fit in at Real Madrid? 
 Past precedent doesn’t exactly paint a rosy picture for the 16-year-old. Andrew Headspeath | Share on Facebook Share on X Add us as a preferred source JJ Gabriel (left) could soon be working under José Mourinho at Real Madrid. | Zohaib Alam/Manchester United/Getty Images (Gabriel), Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty Images (Mourinho) The mini-saga regarding the future of JJ Gabriel appears to be speeding toward a conclusion with Real Madrid reportedly close to sealing a deal for the teenage prodigy.
--> The mini-saga regarding the future of JJ Gabriel appears to be speeding toward a conclusion with Real Madrid reportedly close to sealing a deal for the teenage prodigy.
 The 16-year-old forward, hyped as one of English soccer’s hottest young prospects, caused a stir after opting to cancel his registration at Manchester United back in September.
--> The 16-year-old forward, hyped as one of English soccer’s hottest young prospects, caused a stir after opting to cancel his registration at Manchester United back in September.
 Thanks to his European heritage—his father is an English-born former Republic of Ireland international, while his mother is Greek-Cypriot—Gabriel is able to skirt Brexit regulations and join an overseas club in the upcoming transfer window.
--> Thanks to his European heritage—his father is an English-born former Republic of Ireland international, while his mother is Greek-Cypriot—Gabriel is able to skirt Brexit regulations and join an overseas club in the upcoming transfer window.
 While every big club around had been name-checked in connection for a player once dubbed “Kid Messi,” it appears as though Real Madrid have won the transfer sprint, with a deal now on the verge of completion. 
--> While every big club around had been name-checked in connection for a player once dubbed “Kid Messi,” it appears as though Real Madrid have won the transfer sprint, with a deal now on the verge of completion. 
 Gabriel has reportedly already traveled to Spain and has been working with a personal trainer, with all signs now pointing to a January move.
--> Gabriel has reportedly already traveled to Spain and has been working with a personal trainer, with all signs now pointing to a January move.
 What Type of Player Is JJ Gabriel?
--> What Type of Player Is JJ Gabriel?
 JJ Gabriel has been making waves for some time. | Zohaib Alam/Manchester United/Getty Images Think of JJ Gabriel as the end-level boss of soccer wonderkids. He started off at a club named “Top Ballerz FC” and went viral for his YouTube skills videos while still in elementary school. He spent time at Chelsea , Arsenal and West Ham academies before joining Manchester United in 2022, where he has gone on to break all kinds of records—including featuring for the U-18s aged 14 and scoring a hat trick in the UEFA Youth League against Sabah earlier this year.
--> Think of JJ Gabriel as the end-level boss of soccer wonderkids. He started off at a club named “Top Ballerz FC” and went viral for his YouTube skills videos while still in elementary school. He spent time at Chelsea , Arsenal and West Ham academies before joining Manchester United in 2022, where he has gone on to break all kinds of records—including featuring for the U-18s aged 14 and scoring a hat trick in the UEFA Youth League against Sabah earlier this year.
 He has close to one million Instagram followers, is already tied to a long-term deal with Nike and is managed by his fiercely ambitious ex-pro dad, who changed his son’s name to JJ Gabriel—his birth name is Joseph Junior Andreou O’Cearuill—for marketing reasons.
--> He has close to one million Instagram followers, is already tied to a long-term deal with Nike and is managed by his fiercely ambitious ex-pro dad, who changed his son’s name to JJ Gabriel—his birth name is Joseph Junior Andreou O’Cearuill—for marketing reasons.
 On the pitch, Gabriel is known as a tricky forward who can play centrally, off the striker or out wide on the left. He has been likened variously to Lamine Yamal, Neymar, Lionel Messi and Arsenal teenage star Max Dowman. No pressure, then.
--> On the pitch, Gabriel is known as a tricky forward who can play centrally, off the striker or out wide on the left. He has been likened variously to Lamine Yamal, Neymar, Lionel Messi and Arsenal teenage star Max Dowman. No pressure, then.
 He has represented England at touth level up to U-17, but has yet to be involved in senior men’s soccer—something he intends to fast-track with his next move.
--> He has represented England at touth level up to U-17, but has yet to be involved in senior men’s soccer—something he intends to fast-track with his next move.
 What’s the Plan at Real Madrid?
--> What’s the Plan at Real Madrid?
 The main reason for Gabriel’s surprise split from United was over a disagreement regarding his pathway to first-team soccer.
--> The main reason for Gabriel’s surprise split from United was over a disagreement regarding his pathway to first-team soccer.
 The teenager’s decision to quit the club emerged after he was not included in the squad to face Sabah in the Champions League . There have been suggestions that he—or people working on his behalf—had previously made requests at United that included training exclusively with the first team, guarantees of first-team appearances and a seven-figure annual salary.
--> The teenager’s decision to quit the club emerged after he was not included in the squad to face Sabah in the Champions League . There have been suggestions that he—or people working on his behalf—had previously made requests at United that included training exclusively with the first team, guarantees of first-team appearances and a seven-figure annual salary.
 The Telegraph claims that Madrid have “put together a projected fast-track pathway for Gabriel towards the first team.”
--> The Telegraph claims that Madrid have “put together a projected fast-track pathway for Gabriel towards the first team.”
 The thinking is that Gabriel may at first have to slum it with Real Madrid Castilla in Spain’s third tier, but the club will accommodate his desire for senior minutes in La Liga matches and the Champions League.
--> The thinking is that Gabriel may at first have to slum it with Real Madrid Castilla in Spain’s third tier, but the club will accommodate his desire for senior minutes in La Liga matches and the Champions League.
 It’s an approach Madrid have regularly adopted with a number of highly rated young players, who have flitted between teams before making the step up to the first team full time.
--> It’s an approach Madrid have regularly adopted with a number of highly rated young players, who have flitted between teams before making the step up to the first team full time.
 Should he complete the move in January, Gabriel might just end up becoming Madrid’s youngest-ever player, surpassing Martin Ødegaard, who made his debut at 16 years and 157 days old.
--> Should he complete the move in January, Gabriel might just end up becoming Madrid’s youngest-ever player, surpassing Martin Ødegaard, who made his debut at 16 years and 157 days old.
 Reasons for Caution
--> Reasons for Caution
 Martin Ødegaard’s journey is similar to that of Gabriel’s. | Victor Carretero/Real Madrid/Getty Images Ødegaard’s Real Madrid story gives reason for pause, amid all the hype and excitement.
--> Ødegaard’s Real Madrid story gives reason for pause, amid all the hype and excitement.
 Similar to Gabriel, the Norwegian arrived to great fanfare as the most coveted teenager around at Madrid back in 2015 and was presented at the Bernabéu in a stripy jumper, alongside club legend Emilio Butragueño.
--> Similar to Gabriel, the Norwegian arrived to great fanfare as the most coveted teenager around at Madrid back in 2015 and was presented at the Bernabéu in a stripy jumper, alongside club legend Emilio Butragueño.
 Ødegaard never managed to establish himself at Madrid, describing his awkward situation in The Players’ Tribune : “With the B team, I wasn’t with them regularly so I didn’t find that connection. In the first team, I was just some kid who came to train. I wasn’t involved in matches. I felt a bit like an outsider. I was stuck in between.”
--> Ødegaard never managed to establish himself at Madrid, describing his awkward situation in The Players’ Tribune : “With the B team, I wasn’t with them regularly so I didn’t find that connection. In the first team, I was just some kid who came to train. I wasn’t involved in matches. I felt a bit like an outsider. I was stuck in between.”
 The future Arsenal captain was shunted out on loan and made only 11 first-team appearances for Los Blancos before leaving permanently in 2021.
--> The future Arsenal captain was shunted out on loan and made only 11 first-team appearances for Los Blancos before leaving permanently in 2021.
 Gabriel may well fare better than Ødegaard ever did. Potential is a lottery. But Real Madrid is, infamously, one of the most ruthless and unforgiving environments for young players. European soccer is littered with examples of players who didn’t quite make the grade at the Bernabéu and have the scars to show for it.
--> Gabriel may well fare better than Ødegaard ever did. Potential is a lottery. But Real Madrid is, infamously, one of the most ruthless and unforgiving environments for young players. European soccer is littered with examples of players who didn’t quite make the grade at the Bernabéu and have the scars to show for it.
 While Los Blancos may offer up a clear-cut plan for Gabriel in the recruitment process, things tend to change in the cold hard reality that comes after. With José Mourinho under pressure to deliver a first trophy for Real Madrid since 2024 in the second half of the season, chances for a 16-year-old may be few and far between in the near future.
--> While Los Blancos may offer up a clear-cut plan for Gabriel in the recruitment process, things tend to change in the cold hard reality that comes after. With José Mourinho under pressure to deliver a first trophy for Real Madrid since 2024 in the second half of the season, chances for a 16-year-old may be few and far between in the near future.
 Madrid also already have the likes of Endrick, Brahim Díaz and Carlos Espí vying for scraps of playing time from the bench, behind Kylian Mbappé, Jude Bellingham, Vinícius Jr and record signing Yan Diomande—a player only three years older than Gabriel.
--> Madrid also already have the likes of Endrick, Brahim Díaz and Carlos Espí vying for scraps of playing time from the bench, behind Kylian Mbappé, Jude Bellingham, Vinícius Jr and record signing Yan Diomande—a player only three years older than Gabriel.
 Gabriel has chosen the most glamorous path, but also the most difficult. If he succeeds at the Bernabéu, he truly will be worth the hype.
--> Gabriel has chosen the most glamorous path, but also the most difficult. If he succeeds at the Bernabéu, he truly will be worth the hype.
